title: August and the Bridge
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1912, Elodie Nakamura, a half-Japanese apprentice to a murdered mapmaker, races to complete the master's forbidden atlas of smugglers' routes before the magistrate's men seize the workshop. A sealed letter implicates Elodie's found-family in a conspiracy they never joined, forcing him to choose between burning the evidence that could save them and finishing the atlas as his dying promise demands. When the bridge connecting the workshop quarter to the city is scheduled for demolition to trap the accused, Elodie must carry the finished atlas across it one last time—exposing the true conspirators at the cost of his own anonymity and the love of the magistrate's daughter, who must decide whether duty or truth will define her.
about_author: Petra Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cartographic collections in coastal libraries, where she first encountered atlases with pages deliberately torn out. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He inks the final coastline of the atlas his master died for, measuring everything by what can be carried in one satchel. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Master Aurel's death ruled an accident. Elodie notices the ink stains on the dead man's right hand were on the left. Beat: first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sera Voss's POV. She audits the workshop for the magistrate's office and finds Elodie's work too precise to be merely an apprentice's. Beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: A Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A courier delivers a letter naming the workshop household in a smuggling plot; the seal bears the magistrate's own crest. Beat: cold fear arriving on ordinary paper.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Shows
chapters.summary: Elodie studies the master's hidden marginalia—routes, names, dates—and realizes the atlas is evidence, not art. Beat: the work transforms from inheritance to burden.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Watch
chapters.summary: Marta the dyer's POV. The workshop's neighbors begin avoiding Elodie; someone has been asking questions door to door. Beat: the noose of suspicion tightening invisibly.

chapters.title: Tea with Sera
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sera returns unofficially; over tea she warns him without saying anything actionable. Beat: two people circling a truth neither can voice.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He walks the old iron bridge that links the workshop quarter to the city, counting its rivets like days remaining. Beat: fragile connection between two worlds.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Her father signs the seizure order for the workshop, effective in thirty days; she copies the date onto her palm. Beat: duty beginning to taste like betrayal.

chapters.title: Burning the Marginalia
chapters.summary: Elodie debates destroying the incriminating margins but cannot—the master's last wish was completion. He hides pages inside map rollers instead. Beat: promise versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Man with the Limp
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A stranger with a naval limp photographs the workshop and questions Marta about 'the Japanese boy.' Beat: being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Sera's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sera discovers her father's ledgers contain payments matching the atlas's smuggler routes—her family is entangled. Beat: the floor giving way beneath her certainties.

chapters.title: Twenty-Nine Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He works by candlelight, mapping faster than care allows; a smudged coastline forces a humiliating redo. Beat: exhaustion and stubborn craft.

chapters.title: An Offer of Passage
chapters.summary: The limping man offers Elodie forged papers and a ship out—if he surrenders the atlas unfinished. Beat: survival dangled like bait.

chapters.title: What Marta Saw
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She witnessed Aurel's real death—a magistrate's clerk, not an accident—but has stayed silent to protect her sons. Beat: guilt finding its voice.

chapters.title: The Letter Answered
chapters.summary: Elodie writes back to the sealed letter's sender, bluffing knowledge he doesn't have, to buy time. Beat: the invisible apprentice learning to move pieces.

chapters.title: Rain on the Copper Roof
chapters.summary: Sera comes to the workshop during a storm; almost-confessions pass between them over drying maps. Beat: love kindling precisely where it shouldn't.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Name
chapters.summary: Elodie deciphers the marginalia code: the clerk who killed Aurel is now the magistrate's chief deputy. Beat: the conspiracy reaching into the seat of justice.

chapters.title: Twenty Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A raid scare forces him to evacuate the atlas through Marta's cellar; he learns the neighborhood will shield him. Beat: belonging discovered under threat.

chapters.title: Father and Daughter
chapters.summary: Sera confronts her father; he admits nothing but burns a ledger page in front of her. Beat: filial love curdling into opposition.

chapters.title: The Bridge Is Condemned
chapters.summary: Public notice: the bridge will be demolished the day after the seizure, cutting off the quarter. Beat: escape routes closing in plain sight.

chapters.title: Fifteen Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He tests carrying the full satchel across the bridge at night and times himself against the tide below. Beat: turning hope into logistics.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice Offered
chapters.summary: The deputy, suspecting Sera, assigns her to lead the seizure—forcing her to raid the man she loves. Beat: duty weaponized against the heart.

chapters.title: The False Completion
chapters.summary: Elodie finishes a decoy atlas with doctored routes and leaves it visible. Beat: the craftsman becoming a strategist.

chapters.title: Marta's Sons
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Her eldest is arrested as leverage; she must decide whether to finally testify about Aurel's murder. Beat: a mother's silence breaking.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The limping man returns with a deadline and a threat against Sera; Elodie realizes the deputy wants the atlas to bury, not find. Beat: protectiveness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Reading by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Sera secretly reads the true atlas's key plate and understands everything—her father's payments, the murder, the frame. Beat: the moment loyalty flips.

chapters.title: The Plan on Vellum
chapters.summary: Elodie and Sera meet on the bridge and draft a plan: expose the deputy at the seizure, using the atlas itself as testimony. Beat: love and purpose fusing.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Elodie completes the final plate—the bridge itself, drawn in gold leaf, every name of the quarter inscribed along its span. Beat: the work becoming a monument.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Marta's frightened younger son reveals the hiding place to the deputy's men for his brother's release. Beat: good people forced into harm.

chapters.title: The Decoy Works, Almost
chapters.summary: The deputy seizes the false atlas and declares the case closed; but Sera reports discrepancies, forcing a public inquiry. Beat: hope rising on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The deputy, cornered, orders the bridge demolished early—at dawn, before the inquiry convenes. Beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Elodie packs the true atlas, his master's letters, and nothing else; Marta gives him her sons' birth records to carry to safety too. Beat: the theme made literal.

chapters.title: Dawn on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Demolition charges tick as Elodie crosses with the atlas; the limping man blocks the far end. Beat: terror and clarity.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera arrives with the inquiry party; the deputy, exposed on the bridge, confesses to Aurel's murder rather than let the atlas burn with him. Beat: justice seizing the law's own hand.

chapters.title: The Bridge Falls
chapters.summary: The charges fire; Elodie leaps the final gap as the span drops into the harbor, atlas clutched to his chest. Beat: survival purchased at the cost of the world he knew.

chapters.title: Testimony in Gold Leaf
chapters.summary: The atlas entered as evidence; the household exonerated, the deputy arrested, Marta's sons freed. Beat: vindication that feels strangely hollow.

chapters.title: Sera's Resignation
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She resigns her commission, choosing truth over the family name, and finds Elodie among the ruins. Beat: love chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He adds one final line to the atlas—not a coast but the bridge, drawn whole again in memory, signed with both masters' names. Beat: grief transmuted into legacy.

chapters.title: August and the Bridge
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. One year later, in August, Elodie and Sera open a new workshop; the atlas is published, the quarter rebuilt around a new crossing. Beat: peace earned, carried lightly.
